vectors.purpose: Minimal source with no range shifts or modifier-boundary differences.
Chart-form range shifts, defaults, same-tick precedence, redundant markers, diagnostics, and exact milli-BPM conversion.
Chart-form range shifts on the applicable five-fret Guitar track.
Chart-form range shifts on the applicable five-fret Bass track.
Chart-form range shifts on the applicable five-fret Rhythm track.
Chart-form range shifts on the applicable five-fret Guitar Co-op track.
Per-difficulty open, all-difficulty tap, forced-HOPO, and forced-strum boundaries plus range shifts and exact tempo conversion.
All-difficulty tap applies to a second charted difficulty and remains active at its end tick.
Duplicate pruning and overlap correction for phrases and notes, with every line in tick order.
Star-power and solo exclusive ends plus flex-lane and freestyle inclusive ends.
Quoted E "solo", E "soloend" and E "ld_range_shift 3 2 4" read like their unquoted forms; same TrackHash as source-chart-unquoted-solo-and-range-shift.
Unquoted E solo, E soloend and E ld_range_shift 2 2 4, the control for the quoted forms.
Quoted E "[mix 3 drums0d]" and E "[mix 3 drums0]" read like their unquoted forms; same TrackHash as source-chart-unquoted-mix-events.
Unquoted E [mix 2 drums0d] and E [mix 2 drums0], the control for the quoted forms.
Overlapping single-roll lanes both remain; same-tick duplicates of one type keep the longest; a single and a double lane on one tick are ordered single first; a lane without notes is dropped.
A late [ENABLE_CHART_DYNAMICS] makes velocity 127 and 1 accents and ghosts only on Expert notes after the event.
The same late event applies to Hard from the event onward too, not to the whole difficulty.
[ENABLE_CHART_DYNAMICS] listed before the note-ons of its own tick applies to those notes.
[ENABLE_CHART_DYNAMICS] listed after the note-ons of its own tick applies only to later notes.
.chart accent (N 35) and ghost (N 41) modifiers apply without any [ENABLE_CHART_DYNAMICS] event.
C17: kicks have no dynamics. After [ENABLE_CHART_DYNAMICS], velocity 127 and 1 on a kick or 2x kick add no flag, while the red and yellow pads still get an accent and a ghost.
A yellow tom marker whose range holds no note (a note sits on its exclusive end) leaves the chart four-lane, so every pad is a tom.
A tom marker covering only a kick makes the chart pro drums, so the uncovered yellow notes are cymbals.
A tom marker covering a yellow note makes the chart pro drums: the covered yellow is a tom and the next is a cymbal.
C18: N 109 flams the kick and yellow at 0 on Expert. The 480-tick length of the marker is ignored, so the red at 240 isn't flammed, and Hard's notes at 0 aren't either.

.mid, four-lane: d at 192, dnoflip at 768, off at 1344: disco, then no-flip disco, then none.
.chart, pro drums from yellow cymbal markers (N 66) at 384 and 960: d at 192, dnoflip at 768, off at 1344: disco, then no-flip disco, then none.
.mid, pro drums from song.ini pro_drums, so yellow notes are cymbals: d at 192, dnoflip at 768, off at 1344: disco, then no-flip disco, then none.
.chart, four-lane: d at 192 then dnoflip at 768 and no off: no-flip disco lasts to the end.
.mid, four-lane: d at 192 then dnoflip at 768 and no off: no-flip disco lasts to the end.
.chart, pro drums from yellow cymbal markers (N 66) at 384 and 960: d at 192 then dnoflip at 768 and no off: no-flip disco lasts to the end.
.mid, pro drums from song.ini pro_drums, so yellow notes are cymbals: d at 192 then dnoflip at 768 and no off: no-flip disco lasts to the end.
.chart, four-lane: dnoflip at 192, d at 768, off at 1344: the later d replaces dnoflip.
.mid, four-lane: dnoflip at 192, d at 768, off at 1344: the later d replaces dnoflip.
.chart, four-lane: d and dnoflip on one tick, in both listed orders: d wins each time.
.mid, four-lane: d and dnoflip on one tick, in both listed orders: d wins each time.
.chart, four-lane: off shares a tick with d (both listed orders) and with dnoflip: off wins each time.
.mid, four-lane: off shares a tick with d (both listed orders) and with dnoflip: off wins each time.
"0 = TS 3 " and "768 = TS 5 " end in a space: the denominator exponent is read only when a digit follows, so both are quarter-note signatures.
A .chart five-lane green (N 5) makes the chart five-lane: orange becomes green, and green becomes blue only in an orange-green chord.
A MIDI five-lane green (note 101) makes the chart five-lane, with the same orange-green chord rule.
Six-fret notes: three white and three black frets, open, a white-black chord, and a forced tap.
MIDI range shifts: bracketed form only, same-tick last wins, a Hard marker, out-of-bounds and malformed markers with diagnostics, omitted size, and an inapplicable drums marker.
C1: without song.ini, .chart [Song] values are trimmed and used, and Year loses its leading ", ".
C1: a .chart Year without a leading ", " is kept whole.
C1: only a leading ", " is removed from a .chart Year; ",2004" is kept.
C1: .chart [Song] "0" and "-1" are unset, ", 0" is an unset Year, and style tags are stripped.
C1: .chart [Song] keys match by case, the first nonblank value wins, a lone quote is removed, and Name "midi_export" stops the reader.
C1: a song.ini [song] section replaces .chart [Song] entirely; its missing keys are unknown.
C1: a song.ini without a [song] section is ignored, so the .chart [Song] values are used.
C1: an empty song.ini is ignored, so the .chart [Song] values are used and trimmed.
C1: song.ini "0" and "-1" are unset, a tag-wrapped "0" is kept, style tags are stripped, and an icon equal to the charter is cleared.
C1: without a charter key the charter comes from frets, and the icon is lowercased.
C1: angle-bracket text that is not a style tag is kept; nested and upper-case style tags are stripped.
C2: song.ini lines, keys and values are trimmed with the .NET whitespace set, including U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000.
C2: one leading byte order mark is removed from song.ini, but U+FEFF inside values is not whitespace and is kept.
C2: .chart [Song] values are trimmed with the .NET set (U+0085, U+00A0), and U+FEFF is kept.
C14: a minimal .chart without song.ini; every metadata field is unknown and the preimage carries version 20260801.
C3: only .chart sections with a note after parsing are members: empty, star-power-only, modifier-only, freestyle-only and event-only sections are not; a kick-only section is.
C3: a MIDI difficulty with only phrases or markers is not a member; a Medium difficulty with only a kick is.
C4a: MIDI track names match in any letter case, including the "part drum" alias.
C4b: of two tracks for one instrument the first wins; the second track adds no notes, difficulties or duration.
C4b: a first guitar track with only a star-power phrase still hides a later T1 GEMS guitar track.
C4c: with several tick-0 track names the last one names the track, as in Clone Hero: PART DRUMS then Drums is not drums, PART BASS then PART GUITAR is guitar, and Keys then PART KEYS is keys.
MIDI track 0 is never an instrument, even when it is named PART GUITAR and holds notes.
C5: a folder with both notes.chart and notes.mid is read from notes.mid.
Six-fret guitar and six-fret keys are canonical members next to five-fret guitar, in SongHash instrument order.
C11: .chart with integer song.ini modifiers: hopo_frequency 100, sustain_cutoff_threshold 50 and chord_snap_threshold 5.
C11: .mid with no modifier keys in song.ini, the control for the other MIDI modifier vectors.
C11: integers parse like int.TryParse: "+250" is 250 and "050" is 50.
C11: "170.5", "1e3", "2147483648" and "103.0" are not integers, so every modifier keeps its default; TrackHashes equal song-ini-modifiers-mid-defaults.
C11: hopo_frequency 70000 is clamped to 65535, a negative sustain_cutoff_threshold uses the default, and "-0" is 0.
C11: booleans read like TryGetBool: eighthnote_hopo "2" and pro_drums "-1" are true, and five_lane_drums "yes" is false.
C11: multiplier_note 103 turns the note-103 phrase into star power; the TrackHash equals song-ini-modifiers-mid-defaults, whose phrase is on note 116.
C11: without multiplier_note a single note-103 phrase stays a solo.
Drums: song.ini five_lane_drums and pro_drums together make the chart five-lane, not pro.
C12: the song duration adds one beat after the last note end and converts it through a tempo change inside that beat.
C12: the song duration starts from the latest note end of any track; each track duration uses its own last note end and no added beat.
C12: at resolution 3 and 25 BPM the conversion lands just above 2400 ms and rounds up once; a track whose last note ends at tick 0 lasts 1 ms.

C12: a MIDI sustain longer than the cutoff ends the content, after a change to 200 BPM. Converting end tick 2400 needs the StrikeCore bit increment (1.9 s becomes 1.9000000000000001 s), so the song lasts 1901 ms.
C16: a .chart at B 140000; its TrackHash and durations equal song-tempo-rounding-mid.
C16: a .mid at 428571 microseconds per beat, which rounds to 140.000 BPM; its TrackHash and durations equal song-tempo-rounding-chart.

C18: .mid flam as note 109 over the same notes; its TrackHash equals song-flam-chart.
